Goldman Sachs raised its Q2 2026 average price forecast for Brent crude by $10 to $76 per barrel and for WTI by $9 to $71, citing expected declines in OECD inventories and Middle East production due to low oil flows via the Strait of Hormuz. The bank highlighted upside risks, including prolonged export disruptions and potential damage to production facilities, noting that if Hormuz volumes remained flat for an additional five weeks, Brent could reach $100, triggering demand destruction to prevent critically low inventories. Brent futures were near $82.57 and WTI at $75.28, both up around 5% in the past two sessions. Goldman also revised its Q4 2026 forecasts to $66 (Brent) and $62 (WTI), and 2027 forecasts to $70 (Brent) and $66 (WTI), while noting a potential downside if Hormuz flows normalize faster.
